threats.title: uv bundled CA store trusts compromised emSign root
threats.headline: uv's vendored root bundle trusts compromised eMudhra intermediates, exposing uv TLS connections to MITM attacks.
threats.summary: By default, uv verifies TLS connections against a vendored copy of the webpki-root-certs bundle that includes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root. Eight eMudhra intermediates that chain to that root have compromised private keys. An attacker with one of the keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname and use them for MITM attacks.
who: Python developers installing packages with uv
threats.quote: An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

threats.title: certifi bundle includes root with compromised intermediates
threats.headline: certifi's CA bundle trusts compromised eMudhra intermediates, exposing requests, urllib3 and pip traffic to interception.
threats.summary: An attacker with one of the keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname.
actions: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

action_quotes.action: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.
action_quotes.quote: Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

who: Python apps using requests, urllib3 or pip
threats.quote: If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle.

threats.title: rustls-webpki may accept distrusted emSign intermediates
threats.headline: rustls-webpki could accept certificate paths through emSign intermediates whose private keys are now well known.
threats.summary: The private keys for these intermediates are now well known. Fixed versions reject paths containing these public keys.
who: Rust apps verifying TLS with rustls-webpki
threats.quote: The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK servers exhaust memory on crafted requests
threats.headline: One unauthenticated HTTP request could crash MCP TypeScript SDK servers by exhausting memory during validation.
threats.summary: Affected servers put no limit on how many array elements and object keys they validated in one request.
actions: Turn on the new tool input element limit, since it is off by default.
Lower the request body size limit to what your tools need.

action_quotes.action: Turn on the new tool input element limit, since it is off by default.
action_quotes.quote: The patched versions add an McpServer option, maxToolInputElements , that is off by default.

action_quotes.action: Lower the request body size limit to what your tools need.
action_quotes.quote: Lower the request size limit to what your tools need.

who: Builders using the MCP TypeScript SDK
threats.quote: One HTTP request within the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust the server's memory, and the process aborted with JavaScript heap out of memory .

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK experimental tasks leak across sessions
threats.headline: Clients sharing an MCP SDK task store could list, read and cancel each other's experimental tasks.
threats.summary: In affected versions, the experimental tasks feature did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks. Only HTTP servers that pass taskStore to McpServer or Server are affected, and the 2.x packages are not.
actions: Stop using the deprecated experimental tasks feature.
If you cannot upgrade, give each session its own task store.

action_quotes.action: Stop using the deprecated experimental tasks feature.
action_quotes.quote: The best course of action is to stop using them.

action_quotes.action: If you cannot upgrade, give each session its own task store.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, remove taskStore , or create one InMemoryTaskStore per session.

who: MCP HTTP servers that use taskStore
threats.quote: Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.

threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Recoverable eMudhra intermediate CA keys let attackers impersonate any website, exposing non-browser TLS clients
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. Six are TLS intermediates trusted by the Chrome, Mozilla, Microsoft and Apple root programs, and two are codesigning intermediates trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of these keys could impersonate any website or service to clients that do not enforce Certificate Transparency or do not consume revocation information.
actions: Update Python certifi to 2026.10.19 or later
Update curl CA bundle to 2026-10-20 or later
Update Homebrew ca-certificates to 2026-09-25_1 or later
Update browsers and operating systems promptly.
Make sure non-browser TLS clients and their CA bundles no longer trust the compromised intermediates.

action_quotes.action: Update browsers and operating systems promptly.
action_quotes.quote: Users should update their browsers and operating systems to the latest versions as soon as possible.

action_quotes.action: Make sure non-browser TLS clients and their CA bundles no longer trust the compromised intermediates.
action_quotes.quote: However, many other clients do not consume revocation information and require software updates to ensure they no longer trust the compromised intermediates.

who: TLS clients outside browsers that do not check revocation
developers relying on bundled CA stores in Python, Node.js, Go or curl
Windows users trusting code signed through the affected intermediates
threats.quote: An attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs could impersonate any website or service.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK bearer auth skips token audience check
threats.headline: MCP servers using SDK bearer auth could accept tokens issued for other services by the same authorization server.
threats.summary: This affects HTTP servers using requireBearerAuth() or verifyBearerToken() whose verifyAccessToken() does not check the audience itself.
actions: Turn on the new expected resource check, since it is off by default.
Reject tokens whose audience does not include your server in your token verifier.

action_quotes.action: Turn on the new expected resource check, since it is off by default.
action_quotes.quote: The patched versions add an expectedResource setting that is off by default.

action_quotes.action: Reject tokens whose audience does not include your server in your token verifier.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose aud does not include your server inside verifyAccessToken() .

who: MCP HTTP servers using SDK bearer auth
Deployments where one authorization server serves several services
threats.quote: Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript client SDK leaks headers on cross-origin redirects
threats.headline: MCP SDK clients followed cross-origin redirects, sending API keys, session IDs and OAuth secrets to other origins.
threats.summary: A server that redirected a request to another origin caused that origin to receive custom request headers, such as an API key, and the mcp-session-id header. On a 307 or 308 the request body also went along, including OAuth token requests with their refresh_token and client_secret.
actions: Rotate API keys and client secrets and revoke tokens if a redirect may have reached a host you do not control.
Do not restore the old redirect behaviour on transports.

action_quotes.action: Rotate API keys and client secrets and revoke tokens if a redirect may have reached a host you do not control.
action_quotes.quote: If a redirect may have reached a host you do not control, rotate the API keys and client_secret your application held and revoke its tokens.

action_quotes.action: Do not restore the old redirect behaviour on transports.
action_quotes.quote: Setting redirectPolicy: 'follow' on a transport restores the old behaviour and the exposure.

who: MCP clients using HTTP or SSE transports
Apps using the SDK's OAuth client functions
threats.quote: On a 307 or 308 it also received the request body, including OAuth token requests with their refresh_token and client_secret .
